short: Multi-view input (M05) is new for video-to-speech but standard on its evidence: 2 speakers, gains overstated (11.4% in Table 1, 26% in text); PESQ only, no listener test (M12).
position: The paper [@kumar2018harnessing] changes one component, the camera input (M05), feeding two OuluVS2 views to a video-to-speech regressor; no earlier video-to-speech ledger paper names multi-view input (Appendix). The design is new for speech output but standard on its evidence: two speakers, no repeats or split stated, best pairs only (Sec. 4.3, Sec. 6). Table 1 gives +11.4% and +12.2% PESQ for 0°+30° over 0° (inference), not the stated 26% and 27%. The 30° to 60° placement rule rests on two pairs; follow-up work by the same group finds 0°+45° best and 0°+60° below 0°+90° [@kumar2019lipper] [concurrent], and a 1.1% gain for 0°+30° on held-out data [@uttam2019hushhush] [later] (inference). The evaluation (M12) is behind: PESQ only, where the systems it builds on all ran listener tests.
